values-decisions.title: Values and choices
values-decisions.intro: Separate outside expectations from the values you want to keep.

habits-growth.title: Habits and growth
habits-growth.intro: Notice delays, priorities, and patterns that already help.

money-priorities.title: Spending priorities
money-priorities.intro: Separate wants, needs, and money habits you can sustain.

money-boundaries.title: Money boundaries
money-boundaries.intro: Check major spending, shared costs, and giving boundaries.

learning-direction.title: Learning direction
learning-direction.intro: Choose the next focus, method, and feedback to test.

project-momentum.title: Project momentum
project-momentum.intro: Find the next step, smaller scope, and a pause condition.

self-priority-now.title: What matters most to me now?
self-priority-now.summary: Separate outside expectations from the value I want to keep.
self-priority-now.focus: Read what matters most now by separating outside expectations from the value I want to protect. Do not state my priorities as verified fact or invent recent choices. Only when useful, briefly suggest checking actual decision records or making a small reversible change in time or attention.

self-expectation-source.title: Whose expectation is shaping my choice?
self-expectation-source.summary: Separate an inherited rule from a value I actively choose.
self-expectation-source.focus: Read whether the expectation shaping this choice feels inherited, repeated, or actively chosen. Do not invent another person’s current demands or my past. Only when useful, briefly suggest checking actual words or decision records and expressing my own criterion in a small reversible way.

self-review-condition.title: What would make me reconsider this choice?
self-review-condition.summary: Name evidence that would strengthen or weaken the decision.
self-review-condition.focus: Define what evidence would strengthen or weaken this contemplated choice. Do not settle the outcome; name a record or condition to check, one reversible information-gathering step, and a stop or review condition before committing.

self-repeating-delay.title: What keeps delaying my start?
self-repeating-delay.summary: Separate missing preparation from a burden I keep avoiding.
self-repeating-delay.focus: Read the delay between preparation I lack and a burden I want to avoid through the meanings. Do not invent past attempts. Only when useful, briefly suggest checking actual records or testing a small reversible start.

self-energy-focus.title: Where should my effort go first?
self-energy-focus.summary: Compare urgent demands with what I want to sustain.
self-energy-focus.focus: Compare urgent demands with the work or value I want to sustain, reading where my effort belongs first and why. Do not invent a schedule or commitments. Only when useful, briefly suggest checking actual records or making a small reversible shift in attention.

self-supportive-pattern.title: What should I keep as it is?
self-supportive-pattern.summary: Notice a repeated action that already supports me.
self-supportive-pattern.focus: Read a repeated action that may already support me and why it matters through the meanings. Do not present a personality judgment or recent example as fact. Only when useful, briefly suggest checking actual records or keeping a small reversible instance.

money-spending-priority.title: What should my spending protect first?
money-spending-priority.summary: Compare an immediate want with an ongoing daily priority.
money-spending-priority.focus: Compare an immediate want with an ongoing daily priority shown in actual spending records. Do not decide affordability or predict a financial result; choose one reversible record or allocation rule and review it when an essential need or actual term changes.

money-want-or-need.title: How can I separate wants from needs?
money-want-or-need.summary: Separate emotional spending from a need shown in my records.
money-want-or-need.focus: Separate emotional spending from a need supported by records and actual terms. Do not label the reader's finances or decide what they can afford; use one reversible pause or recording step and a review condition that would change the classification.

money-sustainable-habit.title: Which money habit can I sustain?
money-sustainable-habit.summary: Choose a repeatable record or limit over a big promise.
money-sustainable-habit.focus: Compare a repeatable money record or limit with a large promise that may be hard to keep. Ground the reading in actual records, test only a small reversible habit, and stop or revise it when essential costs or verified terms are not represented.

money-big-purchase-check.title: What should I check before a major purchase?
money-big-purchase-check.summary: Compare the hoped-for value with actual cost and terms.
money-big-purchase-check.focus: Compare the hoped-for value with the documented total cost, fees, and actual terms. Never call the purchase reversible or decide affordability; the reversible step is only comparing records or verifying return and cancellation terms, and the stop condition is to avoid commitment when terms are missing or change.

money-shared-cost.title: What should we agree on before sharing costs?
money-shared-cost.summary: Clarify responsibility, timing, and changes before money changes hands.
money-shared-cost.focus: Clarify responsibility, timing, and change rules before money changes hands. Check actual responsibilities or written terms without assuming fairness or either person's capacity; make the reversible step a draft or clarifying question, and stop before transfer if a responsibility or term remains unclear.

money-helping-boundary.title: What boundary should I set before giving money?
money-helping-boundary.summary: Separate my wish to help from what I can carry.
money-helping-boundary.focus: Separate my wish to help from a boundary supported by my own records and stated responsibilities. Do not decide affordability or direct a transfer; make the reversible step stating or checking the boundary, and stop before giving money if pressure, terms, or high-stakes consequences remain unclear.

study-next-focus.title: What should I study first?
study-next-focus.summary: Choose one part to test before expanding the scope.
study-next-focus.focus: Read one bounded part of the goal to study first and why, before expanding the scope. Do not invent actual tasks or gaps. Only when useful, briefly add a task condition to check or a small reversible learning test.

study-method-fit.title: Which study method fits this goal?
study-method-fit.summary: Compare a familiar method with what I actually retain.
study-method-fit.focus: Read which study approach fits this goal through the tension between familiar methods and a needed new approach. Do not promise mastery. Only when useful, briefly suggest a small reversible change checked against actual recall, work samples, or feedback.

study-feedback-gap.title: What could unlock this stuck point?
study-feedback-gap.summary: Separate more practice from a need for explanation or feedback.
study-feedback-gap.focus: Read the key clue to the stuck point by distinguishing a need for practice from a need for explanation or feedback. Do not invent an error history. Only when useful, briefly add a question to check or a small reversible practice step.

project-next-step.title: What is the project's next small step?
project-next-step.summary: Find one piece to test before planning the whole result.
project-next-step.focus: Separate the core deliverable from one piece that can be verified next. Check actual requirements or current work, make only that small reversible test, and stop or revise it when the result does not reduce uncertainty about the deliverable.

project-scope-boundary.title: What can I remove from this project?
project-scope-boundary.summary: Separate the core result from work that can be removed.
project-scope-boundary.focus: Separate the core result from work that can be removed or deferred. Check actual requirements and dependencies, make the reversible step a temporary scope cut, and restore or revise it if evidence shows the removed work is necessary.

project-pause-signal.title: What would signal a project pause?
project-pause-signal.summary: Define progress evidence and a pause condition before continuing.
project-pause-signal.focus: Define evidence of progress and a signal for pausing before effort becomes its own reason to continue. Check the project record, set one reversible checkpoint or pause, and review the decision when the chosen evidence or boundary is reached.
